Expressions in Model Equations

Source: R/expressions.R
expressions.Rd

Right-hand sides, root functions and event values of cppODE() and cvode() models and the equations of cppFUN() are character strings in R syntax. Both ODE backends read them alike.

Arithmetic

+, -, * and /, and powers written as ^ or **, as in "k1*A^2/(K + A)". Operators R does not have or reads otherwise are an error: %% (write a - floor(a/b)*b), %/% (write floor(a/b)), %, //, ~, @, and <- without a space, which R reads as an assignment.

Comparisons and logic

The comparisons <, <=, >, >=, == and != and the logical operators &&, || and ! give 1 where they hold and 0 elsewhere. & and | read as && and ||, which they equal on numbers. They can stand anywhere a number can:

  • as a factor, "k*(A > A0)" or "k*(time >= t1 && time < t2)";

  • as the condition of piecewise(), "piecewise(kon, A > A0, koff)", or of ifelse(), "ifelse(A > A0, kon, koff)".

A comparison does not chain: "t1 < time < t2" is an error, write "t1 < time && time < t2".

As in R, ! negates everything up to the next &&, ||, comma or closing bracket: "!A > A0" reads !(A > A0). Write the negation in brackets where it is a factor, "k*(!(A > A0))".

Functions

GroupFunctions
Exponential and logarithmexp, exp2, exp10, log, ln, log2, log10, log(x, b)
Roots and powerssqrt, cbrt, root(x, n), pow(x, y)
Trigonometricsin, cos, tan, cot, sec, csc, asin, acos, atan, acot, asec, acsc, atan2(y, x)
Hyperbolicsinh, cosh, tanh, coth, sech, csch, asinh, acosh, atanh, acoth, asech, acsch
Error functionerf, erfc
Kinks and stepsabs, min, max, floor, ceiling, round, trunc
Switchespiecewise(v1, c1, v2, c2, ..., otherwise), ifelse(c, v1, v2), Heaviside(x), sign(x)

Every function works with every backend and derivative mode. floor(), ceiling(), round() and trunc() have the derivative 0; round() rounds half to even, as R does. At a kink or step the derivative is that of the branch the value takes, forward and reverse alike: sign() and Heaviside() have the derivative 0, and a tie of max() takes the derivative of the first argument, of min() that of the second. In the right-hand side of an ODE model they take parameters and forcings only: of a state or of the time they jump where no root is located, which is an error. Write such a step with comparisons, "piecewise(0, x < 1, 1, x < 2, 2)".

Switches

piecewise() takes the arguments in SBML order: the first value whose condition holds, else otherwise. A comparison <, <=, > or >= on a state or on the time switches the right-hand side, inside piecewise() or as a factor, and so do Heaviside() and sign() of such an amount. The solver locates every such switch as a root and continues on the other branch, so a pulse in time is not stepped over, and the sensitivities take the jump, also where a parameter moves the switch. Where both branches push the solution onto the surface it slides along it, so "v*(x > 0)" is the Km to 0 limit of "v*x/(Km + x)", also with an input. == and != are evaluated as written. Details are in cppODE().

Symbols

time is the independent variable, and pi is the number, as in R; pi cannot name a state, a parameter, a forcing or a variable. Every other name is a state, a parameter, a forcing or a variable of cppFUN(), E included: write exp(1) for Euler's number. Python keywords such as lambda, in or if, and True, False and None, cannot be names.

Further functions

A function not listed here can be requested from the maintainer, maintainer("cppDE"), or as an issue at https://github.com/dModverse/cppDE/issues.

See also

cppODE(), cvode(), cppFUN()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (codegenAvailable()) {
  ## Comparisons and logic give 1 or 0: as a factor or as a condition.
  ##   u: a pulse between t1 and t2, `&&` joins two comparisons on time
  ##   x: decays fast below xc and slowly above, unless mode is 0
  ##   y: produced once x exceeds xc, with powers as `^` and `**`
  eqns <- c(
    u = "a*(time >= t1 && time < t2) - u/tau",
    x = "k*u - piecewise(kfast, mode == 0 || !(x > xc), kslow)*x",
    y = "kp*Heaviside(x - xc)*(1 - y^2) - y**2/(K + y)"
  )
  parms <- c(u = 0, x = 0, y = 0, a = 2, t1 = 1, t2 = 3, tau = 1, k = 1,
             kslow = 0.1, kfast = 1, xc = 0.5, mode = 1, kp = 1, K = 0.5)
  times <- 0:8

  ## The same equations on both backends, compiled together
  models <- list(cppODE = cppODE(eqns, deriv = FALSE, compile = FALSE))
  if (codegenAvailable("cvode"))
    models$cvode <- cvode(eqns, compile = FALSE)
  do.call(compile, c(unname(models), list(output = "expressions_example")))

  out <- lapply(models, function(m) solveODE(m, times, parms)$variable)
  cbind(time = times, out$cppODE)
  if (!is.null(out$cvode)) max(abs(out$cppODE - out$cvode))
}
# }
